sourceVerification.graph: Binary directed adjacency matrix, no loops, no same-direction parallel arcs; antiparallel pairs allowed.
sourceVerification.roles: Every vertex is exactlyS/R/neutral, equal positive sender/receiver counts.
sourceVerification.routes: One sender-labeled trail to each distinct receiver; all original directed edges used exactly once globally. Vertices and intermediateS/R may be revisited. Empty sender-receiver paths are impossible because the roles are disjoint.
sourceVerification.originalGuarantee: At least one valid routing scheme.

proofReview.localBijection: Add one distinguishable virtual incoming port per sender and outgoing port per receiver. Local input-output bijections give a successor graph of edges: source-to-receiver trails and isolated cyclic components. A source trail cannot enter a closed component because its first cycle edge would have two predecessors. Valid schemes recover exactly the same local bijections, including sender-receiver assignments; no S! multiplier/division.
proofReview.twoSlots: Before processingi, contracted segments with both ends unprocessed necessarily begin with a backward edge. They are edge-disjoint, so there are at most two. Preserve the upstream original backward-edge identity after concatenation; its fixed tail plus current terminal vertex determines every future cycle/merge decision.
proofReview.untrackedPorts: An untracked incoming port at the current vertex is source-anchored; otherwise its contracted path would still have two unprocessed ends and would be tracked. An untracked backward-edge start whose tail is still unprocessed can only have become receiver-anchored; if an identity disappeared through merger, that identity's tail was processed at the merger. Thus choosing an already-absent other slot correctly absorbs the path and cannot hide a future self-closure.
proofReview.expiry: When an identity's fixed tail is processed without another tracked prefix entering it, its incoming prefix is source-anchored, so the path is safe to forget. If another tracked prefix enters, the explicit transition first retains the upstream identity. Receiver dummy output safely ends a tracked segment.
proofReview.multiplicity: If c tracked incoming ports arrive, choose c distinct outgoing ports in ordered identity order, then pair the d-c remaining actual ports in(d-c)! ways. Histories with equal endpoints have equal continuation counts; their actual port labels are already counted in the accumulated multiplicity.
proofReview.closures: Choosing one's own starting backward edge closes a component; two cross choices close the union of both segments. Other cross choices concatenate and follow the other selected output. Every directed closed component contains a backward edge and is caught when its last local pairing is fixed.
proofReview.edgeCases: Same backward heads produce two incoming tracked ports at one vertex; same tails produce two available backward outputs and are handled by distinct destination choices. A graph cycle may be traversed inside a valid repeated-vertex trail and is not itself rejected. Isolated neutral vertices contribute0!=1; unbalanced conservation returns0 only after full structural checks.
proofReview.time: Per vertex:O(N^2) no-hit states with constant work;O(N) one-hit states each testingO(N) outputs; one both-hit state testingO(N^2) ordered output pairs. TotalO(N^3) time/O(N^2) space with two rolled layers. Original aggregate bound gives sumN^3<=100sumN^2<=2000000.

Suppressing or inserting that forced transition bijects every complete trail decomposition. Insert between original endpoints for forward arcs, or just before the head for backward arcs; backward count is preserved.
